doc.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023

title: What counts as old music, and music education
summary: He argues the standards weren't old compared with classical music, and blames removal of music from schools for today's state of music.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Right. They say, “Man that music is old.” I said, “Man that music ain’t old. You think that’s old, what about Shostakovich Tenth Symphony? What about you know a German leider, you know, and Mozart? That’s old. What about Gregorian chant? That’s old. Brahms, he was an old man, he used to hang around the college they knew Brahms you know? Ravel was still alive before World War I you know. So that ain’t old you know and now they call it Earth, Wind & Fire old school you know. They’re the most wanted popular band that ever existed — but old. The stuff they’re doing now as a backdrop to hip hop, you know, it’s barely music.

Because they took music out of the curriculum of the public school system you know. And the children don’t know any music. They don’t know music. It’s a miracle that they have accomplished what they have accomplished now, for the black churches you know to be totally null and void.
